messages:
emma: Heads up — weird packing in ap-northeast1. Large training gangs pending, but lots of small stateless jobs occupying GPU shards. Heatmap: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/pack/heatmap?orgId=1
ravi: any recent config changes?
emma: we flipped the node-label syncer to aggressively mirror cloud tags to k8s labels last night. suspect overlabeling: `gpu_role=dedicated` is showing up on general-purpose hosts.
kens: checked catalog: inventory agent logged a few 502s during metadata sync, and it retried with stale cache which included old `gpu_role` values. Those got applied cluster-wide by the syncer.
emma: scheduler then treated those nodes as eligible for gang placement, small pods got scattered into the racks -> fragmentation.
ravi: mitigation: disable label-syncer propagation for `gpu_role` and revert the last sync batch. I'll run `kubectl label node <nodes> gpu_role-` for the mis-labeled nodes in a controlled set.
ops-bot: maintenance: label removal started by ravi on nodes gpu-node-101,gpu-node-109,gpu-node-117.
kens: after rolling back labels on the three test nodes, gang schedulability recovered quickly. pending count dropped to near-zero in ~60s.
emma: follow-ups: 1) infra#901 fix syncer backoff and validate cloud metadata before applying labels, 2) add a whitelist of safe labels for syncer, 3) update scheduler to prefer `binpack_preference=general` for pods with resource < 2gpus, 4) add alert `gpu_label_sync_mismatch` when kube labels disagree with cloud metadata for >1% of GPU fleet.
ravi: also propose a transient admission webhook that rejects pods with tolerations for `gpu_role=dedicated` unless explicitly from known workloads.
emma: will open the incident note and cc support for any impacted customers in the 03:10 UTC window. Thanks team.
